chunks: Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked about the skins of dead animals in which milk, water, and clarified butter are placed: what is your view regarding it?
So he said: “There is no harm in putting in them whatever you wish of water, milk, or clarified butter, and performing wudu (ablution) from it, and drinking; but do not pray in them.”

key_terms.السَّمْنُ: clarified butter stored in the skins
key_terms.الْمَاءُ: water kept in the skins and used from them

ai.seo_question: Can water, milk, or clarified butter be kept in the skin of a dead animal, and may one use it for wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about using skins of dead animals as containers for liquids such as water, milk, and clarified butter. It permits benefiting from them in such uses, including taking wudu (ablution) from what they contain and drinking from it, while prohibiting praying in them.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.15 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) was asked about the skins of dead animals used to hold milk, water, or clarified butter.

Imam (as) said: "There is no harm in putting whatever you like in them—water, milk, or clarified butter—and using it for ablution and drinking. However, do not pray in it (i.e., in clothes made from it)”.
